2026-11-01-01.headline: Nasdaq ends October down 5.3% after an AI-stock sell-off, with Intel down 29% and chip stocks down more than 8% on Friday
numbers: Nasdaq Composite: -2.9% on Friday, -5.3% in October
Alphabet: -12% on Thursday, worst day on record
Semiconductor ETF: more than -8% on Friday
2026-11-01-01.soWhat: Investors have paid high prices for companies expected to profit from artificial intelligence, so a weak outlook or a spending warning from one large company now moves the whole group. The cost of building data centers is rising faster than the revenue it brings in for some firms, and that is what the market is now questioning. Chip designers, equipment makers and cloud providers lose the most when that doubt spreads, while defensive sectors such as health care and consumer staples gain as investors rotate. The open question is whether the coming Apple and AMD reports show spending turning into sales.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance: Markets News, Oct. 30, 2026
CNBC: Stock market outlook for Nov. 2-6, 2026

2026-11-01-01.summary: US stocks fell sharply on Friday, October 30. The S&P 500 closed at 7,580.07, down 1.82%, the Nasdaq Composite fell about 2.9% to 25,437, and the Dow lost about 1.1%. The Nasdaq dropped 5.3% for October, its worst month since March 2025, while the Dow gained 1.7%. Intel fell about 29% after a weak fourth-quarter forecast, Alphabet had already fallen 12% on Thursday, its worst one-day drop on record, and Amazon's revenue and free cash flow disappointed. A semiconductor ETF lost more than 8% on the day, and money moved toward health care and consumer staples.

2026-11-01-02.headline: Thrive Holdings agrees to take home-security company ADT private in a deal valued at $15.3 billion including debt
numbers: Price: $10.00 per share in cash (45.6% premium)
2026-11-01-02.soWhat: ADT earns recurring fees for monitoring homes and small businesses, which gives it steady cash that can support a lot of debt. The gap between the $7.6 billion equity value and the $15.3 billion total value shows how much of the price is borrowing the buyer takes on, roughly $7.7 billion. Thrive says it buys established companies and upgrades them with technology, so the logic is to cut costs and add services to a customer base that already pays every month. Rivals such as cable companies, Amazon's Ring and Google Nest compete for the same homes. The open question is whether a higher bid appears during the go-shop period.

sources.title: ADT press release (SEC 8-K)

2026-11-01-02.summary: Thrive Holdings, a permanent-capital holding company, agreed to buy ADT for $10.00 per share in cash, a 45.6% premium to the $6.87 closing price on October 27. The price values ADT's equity at about $7.6 billion and the whole company, including debt, at $15.3 billion. Funds managed by Apollo Global Management are the only source of financing, and there is no financing condition. ADT may seek rival offers until November 28 under a go-shop clause, and closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027 after a shareholder vote and US antitrust clearance. ADT will become the base of Thrive's smart-home security business.

2026-11-01-03.headline: AstraZeneca's cancer sales grow 18% and lift nine-month revenue to $46.9 billion, while older heart and diabetes drugs shrink
2026-11-01-03.soWhat: A drugmaker's growth depends on new patented products replacing older ones whose protection ends, and AstraZeneca shows both sides at once: cancer drugs growing at double digits while older medicines fall. The Summit stake and the cost program show how large drug companies buy outside science and trim overhead to protect profit as that handoff happens. China's volume-based buying is a reminder that government purchasing can cut prices on mature drugs. The pipeline had four trial setbacks this year, so the open question is how many of the 12 positive late-stage results turn into approved products.

sources.title: AstraZeneca 9M and Q3 2026 results (SEC 6-K)

2026-11-01-03.summary: AstraZeneca reported nine-month revenue of $46.9 billion, up 8%, and third-quarter revenue of $16.2 billion, up 7%. Oncology sales rose 18% to $21.9 billion and now make up 47% of revenue, while the BioPharmaceuticals unit fell 2% because Farxiga and Brilinta lost patent exclusivity and China began volume-based buying. Rare disease grew 12%. The company kept its 2026 outlook for revenue to grow by a mid-to-high single-digit percentage and core earnings per share by a low double-digit percentage. It also announced a $2 billion investment in Summit Therapeutics for about 12% of its shares and a cost program targeting $1.5 billion of yearly savings.

2026-11-01-04.headline: Wall Street enters a week of midterm elections, Apple earnings and a jobs report with profits up about 30% but unusually thin beats
2026-11-01-04.soWhat: Strong growth with small beats means expectations were already high, so stocks need a stronger outlook, not just good results, to rise. A weak jobs number could ease pressure for a rate hike, but strong inflation keeps that debate open after the Fed's 10-2 vote this week. The election matters for specific industries: analysts say a Democratic sweep could mean slower defense spending, more pressure on drug prices and new rules for data centers. Most investors expect little market impact, so the open question is whether the AI spending doubts of the past week matter more than politics.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market outlook for Nov. 2-6, 2026

2026-11-01-04.summary: Corporate profits are strong going into the week of November 2. FactSet projects S&P 500 earnings growth of about 30% for the third quarter, but companies are beating estimates by only 1.4% on average, against 7.5% over five years, with Meta and Alphabet pulling the figure down. 138 S&P 500 companies report this week, including Apple and Palantir on Monday. The October jobs report is due Friday: analysts expect 55,000 new jobs and unemployment at 4.2%, after September added just 29,000. Midterm elections are on Tuesday, and polls show Democrats have a chance at both the House and Senate.

2026-11-01-05.headline: Burger King's US sales jump 8.4% while Popeyes slips 1.8%, leaving Restaurant Brands' growth uneven
2026-11-01-05.soWhat: Restaurant Brands mostly franchises its restaurants and collects royalties on franchisee sales, so a rise in comparable sales flows into its revenue with little added cost. That is why Burger King's turnaround matters more than any single quarter's net income, which was boosted by a one-time tax item. Popeyes' decline shows how one brand can offset gains elsewhere in a multi-brand portfolio. The company still carries debt at 4.0 times earnings, so continued sales growth is what lets it keep paying dividends and reducing leverage.

sources.title: Restaurant Brands International Q3 2026 results (SEC 8-K)

2026-11-01-05.summary: Restaurant Brands International reported third-quarter global comparable sales up 3.8% and system-wide sales of $13.0 billion. Burger King US comparable sales rose 8.4%, Tim Hortons rose 1.5% (Canada 1.8%), international rose 3.9% and Popeyes fell 1.8% (US 2.2%). Adjusted operating income rose to $737 million, up 6.7% on an organic basis, and net leverage fell to 4.0 times from 4.4 times. Reported net income jumped to $704 million, helped mainly by a $133 million tax benefit, and the company kept its 2026 targets, including 8% organic operating income growth.

2026-11-02-01.headline: Marvell Technology agrees to buy optical-components maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion
2026-11-02-01.soWhat: AI data centers are running into a bandwidth wall, so moving data with light (optical links) is becoming as important as the chips that process it. Marvell is betting that owning the lasers and optical parts, not just the custom AI chips and interconnect silicon, lets it sell a bigger bundle to cloud customers and compete with Broadcom and Nvidia. The risk is price and timing: paying a premium in stock while AI-linked shares are falling, for a deal that will not close for more than a year. The open question is whether optical demand keeps outrunning supply long enough to justify $115 billion.

sources.title: Marvell to buy Lumentum in $115 billion deal in AI data-center bet (MarketScreener/Reuters)
CNBC: Stock market today, Nov. 2, 2026

2026-11-02-01.summary: Marvell will pay 4.5 of its own shares for each Lumentum share, or $1,132 per share, a 23.9% premium to Lumentum's price on October 28 before talks were reported. The equity value is about $102.5 billion, or $115 billion including debt, and Lumentum holders would own roughly 33% of the combined company. Marvell expects the deal to close in the first half of 2028 and to deliver more than $1 billion of annual cost savings. It is Marvell's largest purchase since the $10 billion Inphi deal in 2021. Lumentum shares fell more than 10% and Marvell more than 5% in early trading.

2026-11-02-02.headline: Oil drops about 6% as US-Iran diplomacy advances, even though OPEC+ keeps December output targets unchanged
2026-11-02-02.soWhat: Oil is trading on the odds of reopening the Strait of Hormuz, not on OPEC+ quotas, which barely matter while Gulf exports are physically disrupted. A deal would cut crude prices, but it would also shrink the refining margins that lifted oil majors' profits this quarter, so producers, refiners and shipowners do not all win or lose together. Importing countries and airlines gain from lower fuel costs, while US shale producers lose some of the windfall. The open question is whether talks hold, since prices have swung on every headline.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market today, Nov. 2, 2026
Voice of Emirates: Oil prices decline on Monday

2026-11-02-02.summary: Brent crude fell more than 6% to about $106 a barrel and US WTI fell to about $97 on reports that the United States and Iran were pursuing talks to end an eight-month conflict. Iran's supreme leader reportedly gave the government some authority to negotiate, and Iranian and Qatari officials held three days of talks. OPEC+ left its December production targets unchanged. The drop follows an October in which crude rose more than 10%, so prices are still far above where they were before the conflict.

2026-11-02-03.headline: US stocks rebound as oil falls, with elections and a jobs report ahead; European factories keep expanding
2026-11-02-03.soWhat: Markets are being pulled by three forces at once: oil and inflation, AI-spending doubts, and political and data events. A fall in oil helps because lower inflation reduces pressure on central banks to keep raising rates, which supports valuations. The October rotation shows investors paying for stable earners over AI growth stories after a sharp tech sell-off. Strong European and UK factory data also cuts the other way, since faster activity can keep rate-hike talk alive at the Bank of England.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market today, Nov. 2, 2026

2026-11-02-03.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.6%, the Nasdaq 0.8% and the Dow 537 points, or 1%, in Monday trading as lower oil prices eased inflation worries. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq had both lost ground in October on AI spending worries, the Nasdaq's worst month since March 2025, while the Dow gained almost 2% as investors rotated toward defensive sectors such as healthcare. US midterm elections are on Tuesday and the monthly jobs report is due this week. In Europe, the eurozone manufacturing PMI came in at 52.7, above the 52.4 forecast and just under September's four-year high of 52.9, and UK factory output grew at its fastest pace in more than two years.

2026-11-02-04.headline: Kioxia shares fall about 14% after it says flash-memory price gains are stalling
numbers: NAND price growth: mid-20% range vs ~70% prior quarter
Guided operating profit: 2 trillion yen vs 2.35 trillion expected
2026-11-02-04.soWhat: Memory is a commodity business where profits depend on price much more than on volume. Prices were being driven up by AI data centers buying storage, and a slowdown in price growth, even from very high levels, is read as a sign the shortage is peaking. That matters for makers, which have earned very high margins, and for buyers such as phone, PC and server makers, which would gain from easier pricing. It also adds to October's worry that AI-linked chip stocks had priced in too much.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market today, Nov. 2, 2026
ZeroHedge (relaying Bloomberg): Flash crash, Kioxia warns NAND price surge ending

2026-11-02-04.summary: Kioxia, the Japanese flash-memory maker, said average selling prices for NAND rose in the mid-20% range in the three months to September, versus about 70% the quarter before. It guided operating profit of 2 trillion yen for the current quarter, below the 2.35 trillion yen analysts expected, and its shares fell about 14%. A Bloomberg report relayed by ZeroHedge said its fab partner Sandisk fell as much as 8%.

2026-11-02-05.headline: BP's third-quarter underlying profit jumps to $8.5 billion as record refining margins help, and net debt falls to $13.9 billion
2026-11-02-05.soWhat: Refining margins hit records because war-related outages and strikes on Russian refineries left fuel short, and the Gulf Coast 3-2-1 crack spread reached an all-time high of $72.64 in September. BP, like Exxon and Chevron, used the windfall to repair its balance sheet rather than increase payouts, which shows how cautious oil majors are about a margin spike that could reverse. Impairments on low-carbon assets show the other side of the strategy shift away from renewables. The open question is how quickly margins normalize if Hormuz reopens.

sources.title: Political.org: Exxon, Chevron and BP beat third-quarter forecasts
Egypt Oil & Gas: bp posts $8.5 Bn underlying profit in Q3 2026

2026-11-02-05.summary: BP reported underlying replacement-cost profit of $8.5 billion, against $2.2 billion a year earlier, $5.7 billion in the second quarter and a consensus of $6.2 billion. The gain came mainly from much higher refining margins and a stronger gas and marketing trading result. It also booked about $4 billion of impairments, mostly on transition businesses such as offshore wind and solar developer Lightsource bp. Net debt fell to $13.9 billion from $22.3 billion at the end of June. CEO Meg O'Neill said the dividend remains the first call on cash, with buybacks only when appropriate, and that refining margins are starting to soften.

2026-11-02-06.headline: Oracle offers $10 billion of common stock as investors question the cost of AI infrastructure
2026-11-02-06.soWhat: Building data centers for AI customers costs far more than the cash these businesses generate today, so even large companies are turning to debt and new shares. Selling stock dilutes existing holders but avoids adding to Oracle's debt load, which markets have been watching closely. It shows that the AI build-out is now limited by financing as much as by chips and power. Lenders and shareholders will push for proof that contracted demand turns into cash.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market today, Nov. 2, 2026
Bisnow: Oracle aims to calm investor fears with $50B AI funding plan

2026-11-02-06.summary: Oracle launched an offering of $10 billion of common stock, with Wells Fargo, Citigroup and BNP Paribas among the bookrunners, and its shares fell more than 2.5% in premarket trading. The raise fits a financing plan Oracle laid out earlier this year to fund about $45 billion to $50 billion of new cloud capacity, roughly half through equity. The sale comes in the same week Alphabet reported negative free cash flow and Amazon guided to roughly $220 billion of capex.

2026-11-02-07.headline: Jio Platforms posts its first results as a listed company: profit up 14% and EBITDA margin at 54.1%
2026-11-02-07.soWhat: Telecom is a scale business: once the network is built, extra subscribers and data use drop through to profit, which is why margins can expand while revenue grows around 11%. Jio's high 5G share shows how a single operator can shift a whole market to a new technology and then monetize it through data use and gradual price increases. Its listing gives investors a direct way to own India's fastest-growing digital consumer base. The risk is that price competition or regulators cap how fast ARPU can rise.

sources.title: Mint via TradingView: Jio Platforms shares jump 3% post strong Q2 results

2026-11-02-07.summary: Jio Platforms, India's largest mobile operator, reported September-quarter revenue of Rs 40,475 crore, up 11% from a year earlier, and net profit of Rs 8,389 crore, up 14%. EBITDA rose 17% and the margin widened by 2.5 percentage points to 54.1%. Average revenue per user was Rs 218.8, a modest rise, with promotions on fixed broadband holding it back. It added 9.1 million net subscribers, has 300 million 5G users, and 5G now carries 56% of wireless data traffic. Shares rose as much as 3% after the report, following a debut on October 28 at a 21% premium to the IPO price.

2026-11-03-01.headline: Apple's September-quarter revenue rises 12% to a record $114.5 billion on iPhone and Mac strength
2026-11-03-01.soWhat: iPhone is still about half of Apple's revenue, so the upgrade cycle largely sets the company's results, while the steadily growing Services line adds a recurring layer on top of the installed base of devices. The margin is the thing to watch: about a point of the 47.9% came from one-off tariff refunds, and memory chip costs have been the main source of margin pressure. That ties a consumer-device maker to the same memory cycle that drives chipmakers such as Kioxia and SK hynix. The open question is whether strong China demand holds up as the cost of components keeps rising.

2026-11-03-01.summary: Apple reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12% and a record for a September quarter, in its first report under CEO John Ternus. iPhone revenue was $57.6 billion, up about 17%, and Services reached an all-time high of $31.6 billion, up about 10%. Mac sales jumped about 24% to $10.8 billion while iPad fell about 10% to $6.2 billion. Greater China was the fastest-growing region at $17.5 billion, up about 21%. Gross margin was 47.9%, including roughly one point from tariff refunds, and diluted earnings per share rose 14% to $2.10.

2026-11-03-02.headline: Palantir's revenue nearly doubles to $2.31 billion as US commercial sales pass government sales for the first time
2026-11-03-02.soWhat: The mix shift matters: Palantir began as a government supplier, and companies buying its AI software now bring in more US revenue than agencies do. A 62% adjusted operating margin shows how software costs little to deliver once the product is built and sold. The gap between 96% revenue growth and 6% growth in total contract value suggests revenue is catching up with earlier signings. The open question is whether new bookings accelerate enough to keep growth near this pace.

2026-11-03-02.summary: Palantir reported third-quarter revenue of $2.313 billion, up 96% from a year earlier and 20% from the prior quarter. US commercial revenue rose 148% to $984 million, overtaking US government revenue, which grew 96% to $953 million. Adjusted operating margin was 62% and net income was $1.128 billion. The company raised its 2026 revenue forecast to about $8.53 billion and its US commercial forecast to more than $3.559 billion. Total contract value grew only 6% to $2.918 billion.

2026-11-03-03.headline: Marathon Petroleum earns $7.4 billion in a quarter as its refining margin hits $45.70 a barrel, and sells two northern refineries for $4.2 billion
2026-11-03-03.soWhat: A refiner earns the gap between what it pays for crude and what it sells fuel for, multiplied by the barrels it processes, so a margin that is more than two and a half times last year's, on a plant running flat out, produces a profit several times larger. Product supply has been tight while Gulf flows are disrupted, which widens that gap. Selling smaller inland refineries to reinvest on the Gulf Coast concentrates the company where plants are larger and can reach export markets. The open question is how long margins last: crude fell 7.6% on Monday on hopes of a US-Iran deal, and a reopening of Gulf shipping would ease product tightness.

2026-11-03-03.summary: Marathon Petroleum reported third-quarter net income of $7.4 billion, or $26.59 a share, against $1.4 billion a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA was $11.7 billion, up from $3.2 billion. Its refining and marketing margin was $45.70 a barrel, up from $17.60, and its refineries ran at 100% of crude capacity. It agreed to sell the St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries and related midstream assets for $4.2 billion, with $3.45 billion going to Marathon and $750 million to its pipeline affiliate MPLX. It returned $3.3 billion to shareholders, raised its dividend 10% and added $5 billion to its buyback authorization.

2026-11-03-04.headline: Pfizer raises its 2026 revenue outlook to $62 to $64 billion as new products offset the fading COVID franchise
2026-11-03-04.soWhat: Big pharma has to keep replacing revenue as older products fade, and Pfizer shows the pattern: the pandemic drugs shrink quickly while cancer, heart and other medicines, many bought or licensed from smaller developers, carry growth. Flat reported revenue hides a business growing 7% without COVID products. Paying for outside assets, such as the Innovent deal, hits earnings up front through charges but is how large drugmakers refill pipelines. The open question is whether launches grow fast enough to offset patent expiries later in the decade.

sources.title: Pfizer 8-K: Q3 2026 results

2026-11-03-04.summary: Pfizer's third-quarter revenue was $16.6 billion, roughly flat, and adjusted earnings per share were $0.87, unchanged. Excluding the COVID products Comirnaty and Paxlovid, revenue grew 7%, and launched and acquired products grew 32%. Paxlovid fell 63% and Comirnaty 29%, while Eliquis rose 25% and the cancer drug Padcev rose 55%. The company raised 2026 revenue guidance to $62.0 to $64.0 billion from $60.5 to $62.5 billion, and adjusted EPS guidance to $2.95 to $3.05, which absorbs about $0.10 from a $650 million charge tied to its Innovent Biologics deal.

2026-11-03-05.headline: US factory activity expands for a tenth month with the ISM index at 55.5, while construction spending falls 1.9%
2026-11-03-05.soWhat: A reading above 50 means more factories are growing than shrinking, so manufacturers are still gaining, and a prices-paid reading of 75 means input costs are still rising quickly. That keeps pressure on inflation and explains why markets are pricing a possible rate rise rather than a cut. High borrowing costs show up first in building, where spending fell sharply. The open question is whether the drop in oil prices begins to pull the prices-paid gauge down in the months ahead.

2026-11-03-05.summary: The ISM manufacturing index rose to 55.5 in October from 54.5, beating the 54.5 forecast, and has now signaled expansion for ten straight months. Its production gauge rose to 59.0, the highest since November 2021, while the prices-paid gauge eased to 75.2 from 77.9. A separate S&P Global US manufacturing index eased to 54.9 from 55.9. September construction spending fell 1.9% against an expected 0.4% gain, the steepest drop since April 2020. Futures priced about a 72% chance of a Fed rate rise in December.

2026-11-03-06.headline: A $6.3 billion theft from Binance, linked by analysts to North Korean hackers, is the largest crypto heist on record
2026-11-03-06.soWhat: Exchanges hold customer assets in a small number of large wallets, so one security failure can threaten the whole business, and confidence that customers can withdraw in full is what prevents a run. Covering the loss from its own balance sheet shows Binance's scale, and the modest 2% outflow suggests most customers stayed. State-backed hacking is a growing funding source for sanctioned governments, which raises pressure on regulators to set tougher custody and security standards. The open question is how much of the stolen money can be recovered.

2026-11-03-06.summary: Hackers moved about $6.3 billion out of Binance in roughly 20 minutes across ten blockchains. Reports say about $3 billion was frozen, and Binance says it will cover all customer losses and had covered about 95% of the stolen assets by Monday. One report puts net withdrawals after service resumed at $3.6 billion, about 2% of customer holdings. Early findings point to a compromised employee laptop.

2026-11-03-07.headline: AI hardware stocks slide as spending worries return, with AMD down 7.5% and Micron down 5.8%
2026-11-03-07.soWhat: Chip, memory and storage makers sell into a small number of customers who are spending borrowed or newly raised money, so doubts about how that spending is financed hit suppliers first. Oracle selling stock and a reported smaller raise at OpenAI both suggest the cost of funding AI capacity is rising. Memory and storage are especially cyclical because prices swing with the pace of orders. The open question is whether AMD's results and outlook on Tuesday show demand still outrunning the funding worries.

The Nasdaq Composite lost 1.07% and the technology sector was the worst in the S&P 500 at down 2.95%. UK press also reported that OpenAI has cut its pre-IPO fundraising target to $20 billion from $30 billion, a report this site has not independently confirmed. AMD reports results on Tuesday after the close.

2026-11-03-08.headline: Affle agrees to buy ad-tech firm Perion for about $420 million in cash
2026-11-03-08.soWhat: Independent ad-tech companies sell tools to advertisers, but the largest platforms, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta, take most of the growth in ad spending, which leaves mid-sized independents struggling to reach scale on their own. For the buyer, the appeal is added reach in fast-growing channels such as connected TV and retail media. A premium of about a third is typical when a small public company with a depressed share price is sold. The open question is whether another bidder emerges before shareholders vote.

2026-11-03-08.summary: Affle 3i Limited signed a definitive merger agreement on November 1 to acquire Perion Network for $11.70 a share in cash, a 34.5% premium to the October 30 close. That values Perion's equity at about $420 million. The deal needs Perion shareholder approval and is expected to close in early 2027. It withdrew its 2026 outlook and suspended its share buyback, under which it had repurchased 21.3 million shares for $196.8 million. Its stock rose about 31% to $11.41.

2026-11-03-09.headline: EVgo's controlling shareholder LS Power proposes to buy out public shareholders at $2.00 a share
2026-11-03-09.soWhat: When a controlling owner buys out the minority, the owner sits on both sides of the deal, which is why an independent committee negotiates the price. EV charging is capital-intensive because networks of fast chargers must be built before they earn, so a private owner can fund growth without the pressure of quarterly results. A closing price below the offer shows investors doubt the deal will be completed at this price. The open question is whether the committee pushes for a higher bid.

2026-11-03-10.headline: US airline shares jump about 4% as crude's sharpest drop in three months eases fuel-cost fears
2026-11-03-10.soWhat: Fuel is one of an airline's largest costs, so a sharp fall in crude lifts expected profit almost immediately, while oil producers and refiners lose the same amount. Most US airlines do not hedge much of their fuel, which makes their shares move quickly with the oil price. The reaction also shows that investors treat the Gulf disruption as the main driver of the energy price spike. The open question is whether the diplomatic progress is real, since a breakdown in talks would reverse the move.

2026-11-03-10.summary: United Airlines rose 4.80%, Delta 4.08% and American 3.81% on Monday as oil had its sharpest one-day drop in three months on hopes for US-Iran diplomacy. Brent fell 7.63% to $104.77 a barrel and US crude fell 7.36% to $96.46. Energy was the worst sector in the S&P 500, down 3.96%, while consumer discretionary was the best, up 2.41%. Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions, and talks with Qatari mediators continued.

2026-11-03-11.headline: IDEXX lifts its 2026 profit outlook after veterinary diagnostics revenue rises 10% to $1.21 billion
2026-11-03-11.soWhat: IDEXX follows a razor-and-blade model: it places analyzers in veterinary clinics and then earns recurring revenue from the test consumables and lab services that run on them. Each new instrument adds years of repeat sales, so installations are an early signal of future revenue. Investors had worried that fewer vet visits would slow growth, and the 10% organic gain shows testing and pricing are offsetting that. The open question is whether visit volumes recover or stay soft.

2026-11-08-06.headline: IEA data show global energy investment of about $3.4 trillion in 2026, with China the largest spender at $940 billion
2026-11-08-06.soWhat: Who spends determines who builds the plants, grids and supply chains for the next decade, and China outspending the US by about $325 billion a year (calculated) gives its equipment makers and utilities a large home market. Suppliers of turbines, transformers and cables gain from high spending, while countries with less capital face higher borrowing costs for the same projects. Utilities that earn a return on what they build benefit most when spending is high. The open question is how much of the total goes to power networks rather than fuel supply.

2026-11-09-01.headline: Crédit Agricole proposes merging its Italian unit into Banco BPM to build Italy's third-largest bank

Banco BPM shareholders gain a premium and a cash payout but give up some control to a dominant holder. The open question is whether the board and Italian authorities accept a structure that leaves the French group close to majority ownership.

2026-11-09-02.soWhat: Nvidia sells the chips that most AI data centers run on, and the US government controls which of them can go to China, so questions about a leader's contacts touch both investor confidence and export-control politics. Customers and lawmakers will watch how the board handles the review and whether Huang's role in shaping chip export policy is questioned. The open question is whether the inquiry stays a personal matter or widens into scrutiny of Nvidia's China-related sales.

2026-11-09-03.headline: US stocks surge as oil falls about 4%, with the Dow up about 650 points and the Nasdaq up 2%
2026-11-09-03.soWhat: Oil is an input cost for almost every business and a driver of inflation, so a fall in crude eases pressure on both company margins and the central bank. That matters now because markets have been pricing a December Fed rate hike after the strong jobs data, and high yields have hurt growth stocks. Winners from cheaper oil include airlines, chemical makers and consumers; oil producers lose revenue. The open question is whether the move lasts, since talks over Iran and the Strait of Hormuz have stalled before.

2026-11-09-04.headline: Oil slips as Iran talks stall: Brent near $94 after eight months of war, with Hormuz still disrupted
2026-11-09-04.soWhat: A large share of the world's oil and LNG moves through the Strait of Hormuz, so every sign of a deal or a breakdown moves crude within hours, and prices near $90 or above mean producers earn windfall margins while importers face inflation. Upstream companies outside the Gulf, such as US shale and Norwegian operators, gain most from the higher price. Refiners and airlines lose when crude spikes and gain when it falls. The open question is whether a signed deal can reopen the strait for good after earlier attempts failed.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio called Iran's demands outrageous. The war is now more than eight months old, the US has kept a naval blockade of Iranian ports for months, and three US aircraft carriers are in the region.

2026-11-09-05.headline: China's factory-gate prices rise 5.7%, the fastest since 2022, while consumer inflation slows to 0.7%
2026-11-09-05.soWhat: The wide gap between factory prices and shop prices squeezes manufacturers, who pay more for raw materials but cannot pass the cost on to cautious households. It also shows two different Chinas: strong external demand and commodity costs on the supply side, and a property slump weighing on consumer confidence at home. For global buyers, higher Chinese producer prices can feed into the price of exported goods. The open question is whether firms will eventually raise consumer prices or absorb the cost through thinner margins.

Consumer prices rose only 0.7%, down from 0.9% in September, and core inflation slowed to 0.8% from 1%. Gasoline was the largest upward push on consumer prices, but a bigger-than-expected fall in food prices offset much of it. Weak property-market demand is holding back consumer inflation, and the CSI 300 index rose 0.56% after the data.

2026-11-09-06.headline: UniCredit posts record third-quarter profit of €3.3 billion and lifts its 2026 target
2026-11-09-06.soWhat: Profit is rising faster than revenue because the bank keeps costs and credit losses low relative to income, and fee and insurance income reduces dependence on interest rates. A bank earning a 25% return on tangible equity can fund large dividends and an acquisition at once, which is why it can afford to take control of a rival such as Commerzbank. Rivals and smaller banks face a stronger consolidator, as the Crédit Agricole proposal for Banco BPM shows. The open question is how much of the profit growth depends on interest rates staying high.

Tighter rules could slow demand growth for utilities and gas-turbine makers and raise costs for cloud companies, while helping developers who already hold permits. Texas, expected to overtake northern Virginia as the largest data-center market by 2030, is the key test. The open question is whether new rules will mainly shift costs onto the data centers or reduce how many get built.

The Nasdaq fell 11% below its record on Thursday amid worries that costlier borrowing and tighter rules could slow construction.

2026-11-09-09.headline: AST SpaceMobile signs a $1.3 billion deal for Firefly rocket engines and the right to build them itself
2026-11-09-09.soWhat: Launch is a bottleneck for satellite operators, so AST is buying its way toward its own rocket instead of waiting for others. Firefly gains funding and a major customer; rocket providers such as SpaceX lose a potential launch customer. The open question is whether AST can build and fly a new reusable rocket on a late-2028 schedule.

Rivals developing obesity drugs also rose, which suggests the market sees the warning as applying to the whole drug class rather than to one maker. The open question is whether doctors and patients start fewer treatments once the new labels reach them.

The open question is how widely restrictions spread beyond the local votes held so far.

2026-11-11-01.headline: Hotter October inflation pushes the 10-year Treasury yield back above 5% as the Fed signals a December hike
2026-11-11-01.soWhat: A 10-year yield at 5% raises the cost of mortgages, corporate bonds and project finance across the economy, and it lowers what investors will pay today for profits expected far in the future. That hits growth and tech stocks hardest, while banks and insurers can earn more on new loans and bonds. Falling gasoline prices should cool headline inflation in November, so the open question is whether core prices keep running hot enough to force more than one hike.

The 10-year Treasury yield jumped more than 14 basis points to about 5.00%. The S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,520.93 and the Nasdaq 0.74%, a day after the S&P's best session since April.

2026-11-11-02.headline: Anthropic sets its IPO range at $70 to $78 a share, aiming to raise up to $64 billion at a value of up to $1.4 trillion
2026-11-11-02.soWhat: This would be one of the largest share sales ever, and it gives public investors their first direct stake in a leading AI model developer rather than in the chip and cloud companies that supply it. The strategic placement shows how tightly the AI supply chain is linked: chipmakers and cloud providers are investing in a customer that buys their products. The range sits below the roughly $2 trillion some early holders hoped for, a sign that the recent selloff in AI stocks has made investors more careful about price. The open question is whether demand holds up at the top of the range after a week of falling tech shares.

2026-11-11-03.headline: Nvidia's board hires Wachtell Lipton for an independent review of CEO Jensen Huang, and the shares fall another 6%
2026-11-11-03.soWhat: Nvidia supplies most of the chips used to train and run AI models, so investors treat its leadership as part of the AI industry's own risk. A long review raises key-person risk for a company closely identified with its founder, and it lands while Washington is already debating chip export rules for China. Customers are unlikely to switch suppliers quickly, so the near-term effect is on the stock's valuation more than on orders. The open question is how long the review takes and whether it leads to any change in leadership or export controls.

The stock fell more than 4% on Monday and about 6% on Tuesday, and its market value briefly dipped below $4 trillion.

2026-11-11-04.headline: Brent briefly drops below $90 for the first time since August as hopes grow that the Iran conflict is ending
2026-11-11-04.soWhat: Falling crude moves money from producers to consumers: airlines, truckers, chemical makers and drivers pay less, while oil companies' cash flow and budgets shrink. The high freight cost for Gulf barrels shows that buyers in Asia still pay a war premium to move oil, which favors exporters in the Americas whose cargoes avoid Hormuz. US drilling has kept rising, with the rig count at 604, the most since May 2024, so a lasting drop in prices could slow that growth next year. The open question is whether a deal with Iran restores Gulf flows fully or the tanker attacks keep a floor under prices.

Shipping risk has not gone away: drones and missiles have hit at least 16 tankers in the Strait of Hormuz this month, and a supertanker voyage from the Gulf to China costs about $36 to $37 a barrel against about $22.50 from the US. The US average gasoline price fell below $4 a gallon for the first time since July.

2026-11-11-05.headline: A windless cold spell sends European power prices above €600 per megawatt-hour in peak hours
numbers: German Oct average: ~€171/MWh vs €82 a year earlier
2026-11-11-05.soWhat: When wind and solar drop, the most expensive plants still running, usually gas-fired, set the price for every megawatt-hour sold, so a calm cold week lifts power bills across the whole system. That rewards owners of flexible gas plants, batteries and pumped storage, which earn the most in scarce hours, and hurts energy-intensive industry and retailers that have not hedged. Episodes like this are why grid operators pay for backup capacity and why storage investment keeps rising. The open question is how many more of these windless spells Europe faces this winter while gas prices stay high.

December power futures in both countries traded near €200, more than double a year earlier, and Britain's grid operator forecast a supply shortfall of about 1.4 GW. Higher gas prices had already pushed Germany's average October power price to about €171, more than double a year earlier.

2026-11-11-06.headline: CoreWeave's revenue jumps 168% to $3.66 billion and it raises its outlook, but its loss widens on interest costs
2026-11-11-06.soWhat: CoreWeave rents out Nvidia-powered computing capacity under multi-year contracts, so its backlog is a direct read on how much AI developers have committed to spend. The catch is financing: it borrows heavily to buy chips and build data centers before customers pay, so interest costs can wipe out operating profit even as sales soar. Rising Treasury yields make that model more expensive, which is why the stock had fallen so far. The open question is whether contracted revenue arrives fast enough to cover debt costs and $37 billion to $39 billion of planned capital spending this year.

2026-11-11-07.headline: TSMC's board approves up to $500 million each for stakes in Anthropic and OpenAI, plus about $41 billion of new capacity
2026-11-11-07.soWhat: The world's dominant contract chipmaker is taking small stakes in two of its largest indirect customers, the AI labs whose models run on chips TSMC makes for Nvidia, AMD, Google and others. The sums are tiny next to its capital budget, so the stakes are more about relationships and visibility into future demand than about financial return. The $41 billion approval shows TSMC still plans to add capacity despite the recent selloff in AI stocks. The open question is whether investors see these cross-investments as healthy partnerships or as a sign of circular financing in the AI supply chain.

2026-11-11-08.headline: SoftBank swings to a ¥1.1 trillion quarterly loss as AI stocks fall and a US data-center power plan is reworked
2026-11-11-08.soWhat: SoftBank is an investment holding company, so its profits swing with the market value of what it owns, and this quarter the AI selloff worked against it. It has also moved from investing in startups to financing physical AI infrastructure, which means borrowing, prepaying for equipment and taking losses when plans change. Higher interest rates make that strategy costlier: the yield on its bonds rose to about 8.2%. The open question is whether a successful round of AI listings, such as Anthropic's, lifts the value of private AI stakes like its holding in OpenAI.

2026-11-11-09.headline: Occidental beats forecasts and cuts debt to $10 billion, using high oil prices to repair its balance sheet
2026-11-11-09.soWhat: Occidental took on heavy debt to buy Anadarko in 2019 and CrownRock in 2024, and it is using this year's high prices to pay that down instead of expanding drilling. Lower debt cuts interest costs and makes the company safer if oil keeps falling from wartime highs, and management says it opens the way for larger shareholder returns. Its midstream unit earned far less than in the second quarter as the gap between West Texas and Gulf Coast gas prices narrowed. The open question is how quickly cash flow falls if Brent stays near $90 or lower.

2026-11-11-10.headline: FDA approves Bayer's Sunharbo, the first factor XIa blood thinner, for secondary stroke prevention
2026-11-11-10.soWhat: Factor XIa drugs aim to prevent clots with less bleeding than existing blood thinners, a long-standing trade-off that has limited how widely they are used, so the class could become a multibillion-dollar market. Being first gives Bayer a lead over Bristol Myers Squibb and Johnson & Johnson's milvexian, which has had setbacks, and a partial replacement for Xarelto revenue lost to generics. Sunharbo failed in a key atrial fibrillation study, so for now it addresses a smaller group of patients. The open question is how fast insurers cover it and doctors beyond stroke specialists adopt it.

2026-11-11-11.headline: Vodafone raises its profit and cash outlook as Africa grows 13%, while Germany stays weak
2026-11-11-11.soWhat: Telecom is a high fixed-cost business, so small changes in revenue growth swing profits, and Vodafone's growth now comes mostly from African mobile money and data rather than Europe. Germany, its largest market, is still losing customers to rivals and faces a court ruling on 26 November about past price increases, so cost cuts are carrying the profit there. The UK merger with Three is starting to deliver savings. The open question is whether Germany can return to growth or whether Vodafone's European business keeps relying on cutting jobs.

2026-11-11-12.headline: Honda raises its annual profit forecast 20% on hybrids and a weaker yen, despite another ¥485 billion in EV costs
2026-11-11-12.soWhat: Japanese carmakers are being squeezed in China by local EV makers such as BYD, and Honda is responding by cutting EV spending and leaning on hybrids, which sell well in the US and earn better margins today. A weaker yen raises the value of overseas profits when converted back to yen, which helps cover the restructuring costs. The new Ohio plant moves more production into the US, reducing exposure to tariffs. The open question is whether pulling back on EVs leaves Honda behind if EV demand recovers later in the decade.

2026-11-11-13.headline: Sea's revenue jumps 43% to $8.6 billion as Shopee and its Monee lending arm keep growing fast
2026-11-11-13.soWhat: Shopee earns more per order than a year ago because it charges sellers more for advertising, logistics and payment services, which is how e-commerce platforms turn scale into profit. Lending to the same shoppers and sellers through Monee is now growing even faster, and it carries credit risk that rises if Southeast Asian consumers come under strain. Rivals such as TikTok Shop and Lazada compete on price, which limits how far fees can rise. The open question is whether bad loans stay near 1.3% as the loan book grows 60% a year.

2026-11-11-14.headline: TransDigm guides to about 14% sales growth in fiscal 2027 after a year of $4.4 billion in acquisitions
2026-11-11-14.soWhat: TransDigm buys makers of specialized aircraft parts that are often the only certified source, then raises prices, especially on spare parts sold to airlines for decades after a plane is delivered. That is why its margins are above 50%, far higher than aircraft makers, and why it keeps buying more such businesses with borrowed money. Airlines are flying older planes longer because new jets are late, which keeps aftermarket demand strong. The open question is whether defense right-to-repair rules or pricing scrutiny limit its pricing power.

2026-11-11-15.headline: JBS's quarterly EBITDA falls 36% as costly cattle squeeze beef margins in the US and Brazil
2026-11-11-15.soWhat: Beef packers buy live cattle and sell meat, so their margin is the spread between the two, and when herds are small, as in the US now, cattle prices rise faster than beef prices. Chicken grows in weeks rather than years, so poultry margins recover faster, which is why chicken is carrying JBS's profits. Shoppers pay more for beef while processors earn less, and ranchers capture most of the gain. The open question is how long the US cattle shortage lasts before herds are rebuilt.

2026-11-11-16.headline: Barrick files to list its North American gold mines as American Barrick Gold on the NYSE
2026-11-11-16.soWhat: Barrick is separating its lower-risk North American mines from operations in Africa and elsewhere because investors often pay higher valuations for gold mines in stable jurisdictions. The open question is whether the remaining Barrick, with more of its value in riskier countries, ends up trading at a deeper discount.

The open question is whether a new leader can keep Nvidia's pace of yearly chip launches and its ties with hyperscale buyers, while rivals such as AMD and in-house chips at cloud companies try to take share during the transition.

Stocks have been drawn down hard, which leaves little cushion if Hormuz flows are hit again, but returning Saudi and Iraqi barrels add supply quickly once tankers move. For producers, prices in the $85 to $95 range still support strong cash flow; for refiners and airlines, the swings make fuel costs hard to hedge. The open question is whether OPEC's 2027 rebound assumes a reopening of Gulf trade that has not yet happened.

2026-11-12-03.headline: Poland's Orlen becomes the first buyer to cancel a long-term LNG contract with QatarEnergy, citing endless force majeure
2026-11-12-03.soWhat: Long-term LNG contracts work because buyers trust them more than the spot market; a prolonged force majeure breaks that trust and gives buyers a legal exit. Qatar supplied about a fifth of world LNG before the war, so if other European and Asian buyers follow Orlen, QatarEnergy could lose committed demand just as its large expansion is due. US exporters gain most, because they can offer new long-term volumes away from Hormuz. The open question is whether Asian buyers, who rely far more on Qatar, follow Orlen or wait for repairs.

The shift toward enterprise customers matters because businesses sign larger, steadier contracts than consumers. The comparison with Anthropic, reported at about $17 billion of quarterly revenue and a small operating loss, sharpens the contrast as Anthropic prepares its IPO. The open question is how long investors keep funding losses of about $11 billion a quarter before demanding a path to profit.

That gives makers like Siemens Energy and GE Vernova pricing power and multi-year order books, and it is why gas turbines now earn higher margins than wind. Utilities and data-center developers lose bargaining power and face waits of years for equipment. The open question is how long the boom lasts once new factory capacity comes online across the industry.

2026-11-12-06.headline: Siemens books a record €108 billion of orders on data-center and rail demand and plans to spin off its Healthineers stake

Spinning off Healthineers makes Siemens a purer industrial and software company, which investors usually value more clearly than a conglomerate. The open question is whether data-center orders stay this strong if AI spending slows.

Free cash flow hit a record €12.1 billion, and the dividend rises to €5.50 a share. Siemens plans to hand its 34.1% stake in Siemens Healthineers to its own shareholders during fiscal 2027 and raised its mid-term growth target to 7% to 11% a year.

2026-11-12-07.headline: UK economy grows 0.7% in the third quarter, its fastest in more than two years, as AI and software work lift services
2026-11-12-07.soWhat: Stronger growth makes the Bank of England's job harder: it raised rates this month with inflation heading toward 5%, and a resilient economy removes a reason to stop. Growth concentrated in software and AI work helps tech services and commercial property in London, while construction and energy-heavy industries lag. The open question is whether the higher energy bills now feeding through to households slow consumer spending enough to bring growth down next year.

sources.title: UK economy grows 0.7 per cent as AI lifts business investment (City AM)

2026-11-12-07.summary: The UK economy grew 0.7% between July and September, up from 0.5% in the second quarter and about 1.9% higher than a year earlier, according to the Office for National Statistics. Services grew 0.9%, led by computer programming, which the ONS linked to AI and cloud businesses, while production rose 0.1% and construction fell 0.7%. September alone grew 0.2%, against forecasts of no growth. The Office for Budget Responsibility expects the energy shock from the Iran war to slow growth to about 1% in 2027.

2026-11-12-08.headline: RWE's nine-month earnings rise 35% on new wind and solar capacity and strong trading, pointing to the top of its 2026 range
2026-11-12-08.soWhat: RWE shows how a utility in transition earns money from both sides: new wind and solar farms add steady contracted profits, while gas plants and the trading desk profit when volatile prices, like this year's war-driven spikes, reward flexible supply. Sharing big offshore projects with partners such as KKR lets it keep building without stretching its balance sheet. The open question is how much of the trading windfall repeats once energy prices calm down.

2026-11-12-08.summary: RWE's adjusted EBITDA rose 35% to €4.6 billion in the first nine months of 2026, and adjusted earnings per share rose 42% to €2.52, about 85% of its full-year target. Onshore wind and solar earned €1.5 billion and offshore wind €1.1 billion, both up about 20%, while gas and other flexible plants rose 25% to €1.3 billion. Energy trading jumped to €543 million from €150 million and will beat its full-year range. RWE now expects results toward the top of its €5.75 billion to €6.35 billion EBITDA guidance, has 13.5 GW under construction and won German capacity contracts for 2.5 GW of new gas plants.

2026-11-12-09.headline: Lilly wins China's first approval for an oral GLP-1 weight-loss pill, getting ahead of Novo Nordisk
numbers: Chinese adults overweight or obese: more than half
Lilly China supply-chain investment: $3B over 10 years
2026-11-12-09.soWhat: A pill is cheaper to make and easier to ship than an injection, which matters in a market where patients pay themselves and where scale will depend on price. Being first gives Lilly time to build doctor habits and distribution before Novo's pill arrives, and Lilly has committed $3 billion over 10 years to supply chains in China. Local makers of GLP-1 drugs and copies of semaglutide are the main threat to both. The open question is what price Lilly sets, since self-paying patients limit how much it can charge.

2026-11-12-09.summary: China's drug regulator has approved Eli Lilly's orforglipron, sold as Foundayo in the US and UK, for weight management in adults with obesity or who are overweight with a related condition. It is the first oral GLP-1 weight-loss medicine approved in China; Novo Nordisk's oral Wegovy is still under review there, though Novo's injectable semaglutide has been sold in China since 2024. More than half of Chinese adults are overweight or obese, but weight-loss drugs are paid for out of pocket. Lilly shares rose about 3% before the US open.

2026-11-12-10.headline: Western Union walks away from its $500 million Intermex deal over California's conditions, and Intermex says it will fight
2026-11-12-10.soWhat: Remittances to Latin America are a scale business with thin margins, and the deal was meant to cut overlapping agent networks and costs. California's condition to keep every agent location blocks exactly those savings, which shows how state regulators can reshape a deal even after federal clearance. Digital players such as Remitly and Wise keep gaining share while the two incumbents are distracted. The open question is whether a court agrees that Western Union had the right to exit.

2026-11-12-10.summary: Western Union terminated its agreement to buy remittance company International Money Express (Intermex), announced in August 2025 for about $500 million, effective just after midnight on November 12. California's financial regulator issued final conditions on November 10 that included barring cuts to California agent locations and tougher anti-fraud measures, which Western Union said would force material changes to its business model. Every other jurisdiction, 54 in all, had approved the deal, and neither side owes a break fee. Intermex rejects the termination, says it expects the deal to close and has threatened legal action.

2026-11-12-11.headline: Marsh agrees to buy investment consultant Wilshire, adding $221 billion under management
2026-11-12-11.soWhat: Large insurance brokers are building investment businesses because advising pension plans and running outsourced portfolios earn steady, fee-based income that fits next to brokerage and consulting. Wilshire adds model portfolios sold through financial advisers and alternative-investment skills, the fastest-growing part of wealth management. Smaller investment consultants face rivals with more scale and data. The open question is whether clients stay through the change of ownership, since the deal needs their consent.

2026-11-12-11.summary: Marsh agreed to acquire Wilshire, an investment consulting, portfolio and index-analytics firm, from private-equity owners Motive Partners and CC Capital; terms were not disclosed. Wilshire manages $221 billion and advises on $1.6 trillion for pension plans, endowments, foundations and wealth advisers. The deal is Marsh's third major investments move in 2026 after buying AltamarCAM in March, and it is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027.

2026-11-12-12.headline: Munich Re raises its 2026 profit target to €6.6 billion even as third-quarter profit dips
2026-11-12-12.soWhat: Reinsurers have enjoyed several years of high prices after heavy catastrophe losses, and a quiet loss year lets that pricing turn into record profits. Raising guidance late in the year signals that catastrophe losses have stayed below budget. The flip side is that strong profits attract new capital, which pushes reinsurance prices down at the January renewals. The open question is how much prices fall at those renewals.

sources.title: Munich Re Q3 net result declines (RTTNews)

2026-11-12-12.summary: Munich Re's third-quarter net result fell to €1.74 billion from €2.0 billion a year earlier, while insurance revenue rose to €16.6 billion from €14.6 billion. The reinsurer raised its full-year 2026 net profit guidance to €6.6 billion from an original target of €6.3 billion. For the first nine months, insurance revenue rose to €46.6 billion from €45.2 billion.

2026-11-12-13.headline: Corteva cuts its 2026 outlook as Brazilian farmers delay buying, and sales in Latin America fall 31%
2026-11-12-13.soWhat: Brazil is the largest crop-protection market in the world, and its farmers buy on credit against the next harvest. When interest rates are high and crop prices low, they buy later and in smaller amounts, and distributors run down their stock before ordering more. That hits sellers of seeds and crop chemicals, including Bayer and Syngenta, as well as Corteva. The open question is whether the weakness is a one-season timing shift or a longer squeeze on Brazilian farm income.

Corteva cuts 2026 guidance after Brazil weakness (Basis Report)

2026-11-12-13.summary: Corteva's pro forma third-quarter sales fell 9% to $1.59 billion, with organic sales in Latin America down 31% while North America rose 7% and Europe, Middle East and Africa rose 14%. The company blamed weak Brazilian conditions, high distributor inventories and farmers' tight access to credit. It cut its 2026 guidance to adjusted pro forma operating EBITDA of $1.1 billion to $1.125 billion and EPS of $0.76 to $0.80. Shares fell about 8% after the results.

2026-11-12-14.headline: B&M shares jump about 17% as UK sales return to growth and the discounter issues its first full-year profit guidance
2026-11-12-14.soWhat: Discounters make money on high volumes and tight costs, so a return to positive like-for-like sales quickly lifts profit because store costs are largely fixed. Shoppers squeezed by higher energy bills tend to trade down to discounters, which helps B&M against mid-market general retailers. The open question is whether the UK recovery holds through Christmas, the quarter that decides the year.

Why is B&M European Value Retail stock surging today? (Investing.com)

2026-11-12-14.summary: UK discount retailer B&M's first-half revenue rose 3.6% to £2.85 billion and pre-tax profit rose 16.6% to £121 million. UK like-for-like sales grew 3.2% in the second quarter after falling 2.3% in the first, and French like-for-like sales rose 6.5%. Gross margin improved by 0.67 points to 37.2%. B&M guided full-year adjusted pre-tax profit of £280 million to £330 million, and its shares rose about 16.6% to 325p.

2026-11-12-15.headline: Air freight rates hit their 2026 high as the holiday peak arrives, up 28% on a year ago
numbers: Baltic Air Freight Index: +6.6% w/w, 2026 high
2026-11-12-15.soWhat: Air cargo is priced by supply and demand for scarce space, so a rush of goods in a few weeks lifts rates fast, and falling fuel costs then widen carrier margins. Cargo airlines, airlines with large belly-cargo operations and freight forwarders gain; e-commerce sellers and shippers of high-value goods pay more. The open question is how much rates drop after the holiday peak, as they usually do in January.

sources.title: Airfreight rates reach 2026 high on peak season demand (Air Cargo News)

2026-11-12-15.summary: The Baltic Air Freight Index rose 6.6% in a week to its highest level of 2026, and rates are 28.2% above a year earlier, according to price agency TAC. Outbound rates from Hong Kong rose 4.6% in the week and from Shanghai 5.7%, while Frankfurt jumped 9.9%. Rates climbed even though jet fuel prices fell 6.5% in a week. Demand is being driven by shipments for Black Friday, Thanksgiving and Christmas, and by less belly space on transatlantic passenger flights in winter.

2026-11-13-01.headline: IEA says the oil market is swinging back to surplus in the fourth quarter as Gulf exports recover
numbers: Q4 2026 supply: ~105 mb/d, ~1.7 mb/d above demand
OPEC+ October crude output: 41.23 mb/d (97% of pre-war)
2026-11-13-01.soWhat: A surplus forecast from the main agency that tracks oil balances shifts the debate from scarcity to how fast inventories rebuild, which usually pulls futures prices lower over time and squeezes producers that budgeted for $90-plus oil. Consumers and airlines gain if the call is right, while high-cost producers and OPEC+ face pressure to restrain output again. The IEA also flagged that diesel supply remains very tight, so crude and fuel prices can move apart. The open question is whether shipping through Hormuz stays open long enough for the rebuild to happen.

sources.title: World oil market is returning to surplus as Gulf exports recover, IEA says (Reuters via CP24)
Oil Market Report - November 2026 (IEA)

2026-11-13-01.summary: The International Energy Agency's November report says world oil supply in the fourth quarter will average about 105 million barrels a day, roughly 1.7 million above demand, after it had earlier forecast a deficit. Gulf producers are rebuilding exports through the Strait of Hormuz, and OPEC+ pumped 41.23 million barrels a day of crude in October, up about 2 million from September and 97% of the pre-war level. The agency sees 2026 demand falling 2.7 million barrels a day to 102.3 million because of high prices, then rebounding by 2 million in 2027. It expects a 2027 surplus of about 3.8 million barrels a day, and Brent hovered near $96 after the report.

2026-11-13-02.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield climbs above 5.1% as producer prices rise 6.5% a year and Bank of America expects three Fed hikes
numbers: Fed hikes expected by BofA: Dec, Jan, Mar
2026-11-13-02.soWhat: When long-term borrowing costs rise above 5%, every other price in the economy adjusts: mortgages, corporate bonds and the discount rate investors apply to future profits. Highly valued growth stocks and rate-sensitive sectors such as housing and small companies tend to lose most, while savers and banks with lots of floating-rate assets gain. The shift from expected rate cuts to expected hikes also strengthens the dollar, which hurts US exporters and countries that borrow in dollars. The open question is whether inflation cools fast enough for the Fed to stop after one or two moves.

sources.title: Newsquawk European Market Wrap, 13 November 2026
Stock market news for Nov. 12, 2026 (CNBC)

2026-11-13-02.summary: US producer prices rose 0.3% in October, a little below forecasts, but were still up 6.5% from a year earlier, with core producer prices up 5.0%. A day earlier, consumer prices rose 0.4% in the month, and jobless claims stayed low at 200,000. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to about 5.17% on Friday, its highest since mid-October, and the dollar rose past 160 yen. Bank of America now expects Federal Reserve rate hikes in December, January and March, and the S&P 500 fell 0.35% on Thursday.

2026-11-13-03.headline: SpaceX and Tesla could announce a merger as soon as December, in what would be the largest deal ever
2026-11-13-03.soWhat: Combining a rocket, satellite internet and AI business with a carmaker would create one company spanning launch, connectivity, robotics and vehicles, which supporters argue lets Tesla's factories and SpaceX's cash flow fund each other. The deal would dwarf the previous record, Vodafone's $183 billion purchase of Mannesmann in 2000. The obstacles are governance and regulation: Tesla's large China business sits awkwardly next to SpaceX's US defense work, and a change of control would speed up vesting of large stock awards. The open question is how many SpaceX shares Tesla investors would receive and whether they approve.

sources.title: SpaceX could announce $1.5 trillion Tesla merger in December: report (Electrek)

2026-11-13-03.summary: Bloomberg reported on November 12 that SpaceX and Tesla are negotiating price and control in a combination that could be announced as soon as December or slip into early 2027. SpaceX is valued at more than $1.9 trillion after its June listing and Tesla at about $1.5 trillion, and the talks describe SpaceX absorbing Tesla. Both boards have set up special committees, and Tesla's shareholder meeting is on December 3. Tesla shares rose as much as 1.9% on the report, and neither company commented.

2026-11-13-04.headline: Cisco's revenue jumps 24% to a record $18.5 billion as AI data-center networking sales climb 43%
2026-11-13-04.soWhat: AI data centers need huge amounts of networking to connect thousands of chips, and Cisco's numbers show that spending is now reaching the equipment makers that sit beside the chip suppliers. This is good news for networking and optics suppliers and a sign that cloud budgets are still growing, but it also makes Cisco more dependent on a handful of very large buyers. Services barely grew, so the mix is shifting toward hardware sales that can be lumpier. The open question is how long hyperscalers keep raising capital spending at this pace.

sources.title: Cisco Reports First Quarter Earnings (Cisco)

2026-11-13-04.summary: Cisco's fiscal first-quarter revenue rose 24% to $18.5 billion, with product revenue up 32% and services up just 1%. Networking, its largest unit, grew 43% to $11.1 billion as cloud providers bought switches and optics to link AI chips. Cisco now expects about $9 billion of AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers in fiscal 2027, more than double last year. It raised full-year revenue guidance to $74.8 billion to $75.8 billion and adjusted EPS to $5.47 to $5.53.

2026-11-13-05.headline: Hancock Whitney agrees to buy Trustmark for about $3.2 billion, creating a $58 billion Gulf South bank
2026-11-13-05.soWhat: Regional banks are merging to spread rising technology, compliance and deposit costs over a bigger base. Buying a neighbor in overlapping markets lets the acquirer close branches and back-office functions, which is where most of the earnings gain comes from. The price is about 7% dilution to tangible book value per share, which the bank expects to earn back in about 2.8 years. Larger regional players gain scale, while smaller community banks face a tougher competitor.

2026-11-13-05.summary: Hancock Whitney will acquire Mississippi-based Trustmark in an all-stock deal valued at about $3.2 billion, issuing 0.7463 of its shares for each Trustmark share. The combined bank will have about $58 billion of assets across six Southeastern states, with Hancock Whitney holders owning about 65%. Trustmark had $19.1 billion of assets at the end of September. The deal is expected to add about 7% to Hancock Whitney's 2028 earnings per share and to close late in the first quarter of 2027.

2026-11-13-06.headline: Applied Materials posts a record $10.4 billion quarter and guides higher as chipmakers add AI capacity
2026-11-13-06.soWhat: Equipment makers are paid when chipmakers build new capacity, so their orders are an early read on how much the industry plans to produce. Strong guidance says that the AI buildout is now lifting spending on leading-edge logic and memory fabs, not only on the chips themselves. Equipment suppliers and their component vendors benefit, while chipmakers carry the cost and risk if demand cools. The open question is whether export limits on China, historically a large buyer of tools, cut into future growth.

sources.title: Applied Materials posts record $10.41B revenue (Crypto Briefing)

2026-11-13-06.summary: Applied Materials, the largest maker of chip manufacturing equipment, reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $10.41 billion and adjusted EPS of $4.16, both above forecasts. Its semiconductor systems unit brought in $8 billion, up 64% from a year earlier. Full-year revenue rose 21% to $34.45 billion. It guided next-quarter revenue to about $11.1 billion, above the roughly $10.9 billion analysts expected.

2026-11-13-07.headline: US diesel stocks fall to about 99 million barrels, near a 23-year low, keeping pump prices above $6
2026-11-13-07.soWhat: Refiners earn the gap between product and crude prices, so when crude eases but diesel stays scarce, that gap widens and refiners' profits rise. Truckers, farmers, railroads and anyone who ships goods pay more, which feeds into freight rates and food prices. Diesel is tight because Gulf exports of refined products were disrupted and some refining capacity is offline, problems that more crude does not fix quickly. The open question is whether stocks recover before winter heating demand peaks.

sources.title: America's diesel stockpiles are running low (24/7 Wall St.)

2026-11-13-07.summary: US distillate inventories, which include diesel and heating oil, are about 99.3 million barrels, which would be the lowest comparable weekly level since May 2003. The national average diesel price is about $6.13 a gallon, up about 60% from a year earlier and about $2 more than gasoline. Refineries are running near capacity and strong overseas margins keep US exports high, so stocks are slow to rebuild. The IEA said on Friday that tight diesel supply remains its main concern even as crude moves into surplus.

2026-11-13-08.headline: Allianz lifts its 2026 profit goal to about €18.6 billion as asset management offsets higher catastrophe losses
2026-11-13-08.soWhat: Large insurers own asset managers partly because the two businesses are hit by different shocks: a bad catastrophe quarter in insurance can be offset by fee income when markets are strong. Allianz shows that diversification at work, which supports steadier earnings and dividends than a pure insurer. Higher catastrophe losses also tend to push up reinsurance and home insurance prices in the next renewal round. The open question is whether asset management fees hold up if bond and equity markets weaken.

2026-11-13-08.summary: Allianz's third-quarter operating profit rose 6.2% to €4.71 billion, beating the €4.30 billion analysts expected. Natural catastrophes added 5.1 points to the loss ratio, against 0.3 points a year earlier, pushing the combined ratio to 93.8%. Allianz raised the top of its 2026 operating profit range to about €18.6 billion, and its Solvency II ratio was 219%.

2026-11-13-09.headline: Richemont's profit rises 39% to €2.5 billion on jewellery, but shares fall as growth misses hopes
2026-11-13-09.soWhat: In luxury, jewellery has become the most reliable growth engine because it holds value and is less exposed to fashion cycles than handbags or watches. Richemont, with about three quarters of sales from jewellery, has gained from that shift while many fashion groups have struggled. Its main risk is the cost of gold, which raises input costs, and demand from Chinese buyers. Investors now expect so much growth that even strong results can disappoint.

2026-11-13-09.summary: Richemont, owner of Cartier and Van Cleef & Arpels, said first-half sales rose 16% to nearly €12.3 billion and net profit rose 39% to €2.5 billion. Jewellery sales grew 18% to €9.1 billion, while watches grew 9% to €1.7 billion. Sales rose 30% in Japan and 23% in the Americas but fell 2% in the Middle East and Africa. The shares fell 4.2% on Friday as jewellery came in slightly below forecasts and comments on China and gold prices weighed.

2026-11-13-10.headline: US existing-home sales drop 5.5% to their slowest pace since 2010 as mortgage rates top 7%
2026-11-13-10.soWhat: Most homeowners locked in much lower mortgage rates, so higher rates freeze the market: owners do not want to sell and buyers cannot afford to buy. Fewer sales hit businesses paid per transaction, such as real estate brokers, mortgage lenders, title insurers and movers, even while prices hold up. Rising inventory hints that prices could start to soften if rates stay high. With markets now expecting Fed hikes, a quick rebound looks unlikely.

2026-11-13-10.summary: Sales of previously owned US homes fell 5.5% in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million, the lowest since August 2010, the National Association of Realtors said. Sales were 8.8% lower than a year earlier and fell in every region, most in the West. The median price still rose 0.4% to $416,700, and inventory rose to 1.59 million homes, or 5.1 months of supply. NAR put the average 30-year mortgage rate at 7.33% in October, up from 6.86% in September.

2026-11-13-11.headline: Canada plans to invest C$200 million in Woodfibre LNG to raise the plant's capacity by up to 24%

2026-11-13-11.soWhat: Canada wants to sell more gas to Asia and Europe to reduce its dependence on US buyers, and Pacific coast plants have a shorter shipping route to Asia than US Gulf Coast terminals. Adding capacity to a plant already under construction is usually cheaper per tonne than building a new one, which improves project returns. Woodfibre's cost has risen to about US$8.8 billion from an early estimate of US$5.1 billion, so extra output helps spread that cost. Gas producers in western Canada gain a new outlet for their gas.

2026-11-13-11.summary: Canada's government plans to invest C$200 million (about US$140 million) in the Woodfibre LNG export plant being built near Squamish, British Columbia, Reuters reported, citing a source. The plant, owned by Enbridge and Pacific Energy, was designed for 2.1 million tonnes a year, all contracted to BP. Cooling upgrades and floating storage would lift capacity to 2.5 to 2.6 million tonnes, and the owners are exploring a second phase. Operations are targeted for late 2027.

2026-11-13-12.headline: Rolls-Royce keeps its profit outlook and brings forward a £1.5 billion buyback as data centers lift engine orders
2026-11-13-12.soWhat: Rolls-Royce earns most of its civil profit from long-term service contracts paid per hour an engine flies, so higher flying hours translate directly into cash. Its smaller Power Systems unit is now riding the same data-center wave as turbine makers, since operators want on-site generators when the grid cannot connect them quickly. Strong cash flow lets the company return money to shareholders while still investing. The risk is that long-haul flying slows or maintenance costs rise faster than expected.

Power Systems orders rose 62% in the first nine months and its backlog hit a record £8.6 billion, with gas engine orders for power generation nearly tripling on data-center demand. Engine flying hours in civil aerospace reached 114% of 2019 levels.

2026-11-13-13.headline: Nissan's quarterly operating profit falls 96% and it cuts its sales outlook again on China
2026-11-13-13.soWhat: Nissan shows how foreign carmakers are being squeezed in China, where local brands with cheaper electric models are taking share fast. Losing volume hurts because car plants have high fixed costs, so profit falls faster than sales. Nissan's answer is to design cars in China with local suppliers and export them to other markets, using China's cost advantage rather than fighting it. The open question is whether cost cuts arrive fast enough to hit the full-year target.

Revenue rose 8.2% to 3.1 trillion yen. Nissan cut its full-year sales forecast to 2.97 to 3.0 million vehicles from 3.15 million, its second cut since August, but kept its operating profit target. Its restructuring plan, which cuts 15% of the workforce, has saved 365 billion yen so far.

2026-11-13-14.headline: Hapag-Lloyd raises its 2026 profit outlook again as container freight rates climb 28%
2026-11-13-14.soWhat: Container shipping has high fixed costs, so small changes in freight rates swing profits sharply: here a 28% rise in average rates turned a thin quarter into a very strong one. Rates are high because Middle East disruption and weather have tied up ships and capacity, not because demand jumped. Carriers gain, while importers and retailers pay more to ship goods ahead of the holidays. The open question is how quickly rates fall once routes normalize and new ships arrive.

2026-11-13-14.summary: Hapag-Lloyd's third-quarter EBIT jumped to $1.09 billion from $228 million a year earlier, as its average freight rate rose to $1,808 per container from $1,413. Volumes were flat at 3.38 million containers, so the gain came almost entirely from price. The German carrier raised 2026 EBIT guidance to $2.0 billion to $2.4 billion from $1.25 billion to $1.75 billion, saying the fourth quarter is going better than expected. It warned that rates are volatile and geopolitics remain a risk.

2026-11-13-15.headline: Wizz Air's half-year profit falls 67% as fuel costs jump a third despite 26% more passengers
2026-11-13-15.soWhat: Low-cost airlines compete on price, so they struggle to pass higher fuel costs on to passengers and profits shrink fast when jet fuel spikes. Growing capacity quickly can also push fares down, which is what happened here as unit revenue fell. Hedging softens the blow but locks in prices for only part of the year. Airlines with more premium traffic and stronger pricing power, such as large network carriers, are better placed.

Fuel costs climbed 33.7% to €1.24 billion, and revenue per seat-kilometre fell 2.9% while total cost per seat-kilometre rose 4.3%. The budget airline has hedged 82% of its fuel for the second half and expects non-fuel unit costs to rise by a mid-single-digit percentage. It gave no full-year profit forecast.

2026-11-13-16.headline: Telefónica returns to a profit and cuts debt by €1.6 billion after selling Latin American units
2026-11-13-16.soWhat: European telecom operators have struggled for years with heavy network spending and price competition, so many are selling non-core countries to cut debt and focus on markets where they are large. Telefónica's exit from most of Spanish-speaking Latin America leaves it centered on Spain, Brazil, Germany and the UK. Stronger home-market growth and lower debt give it more room to invest or consolidate. The open question is whether European regulators allow the in-market mergers operators want.
